 Home NBA lebron james Kendrick Perkins noticed something about Lebron James vs Celtics for the ‘first time’ ever
 Vatsal Gupta Thu 12 November 2026 11:52, UK Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Follow us on Google Discover LeBron James was found wanting in the Philadelphia 76ers’ marquee game against the Boston Celtics, and Kendrick Perkins noticed something for the first time ever. 
 In what was billed as a fight of the elites, the Boston Celtics dominated en route to a 123-101 win against the Philadelphia 76ers. 
 LeBron James scored just 11 points on an ugly shooting night where he connected just one of his 3PT attempts, finishing with a +/- of -17.
 His teammates weren’t much better, but James’ performances had Kendrick Perkins noticing something for the very first time.
 Kendrick Perkins on LeBron James
 Usually, these are the kind of games where James’ light shines the brightest and he takes over through sheer talent and mentality.
 There was nothing of the sort against the Celtics as a much younger and athletic side ran rings around the 76ers and James.
 It is only one game, and it’s not wise to bet against James because he’s so driven as an athlete, but on the basis of that one game as evidence, count Perkins among doubters.
 Speaking on ESPN , Perkins said that for the first time, James looked “old” in his career.
 He said: “LeBron looked old for the first time. No, seriously, for the first time in 20-plus years, he looked old last night. And this is a prime example of why I’ve been begging and pleading for LeBron James to play more of the centre position. If I’m Nick Nurse, I stagger the minutes because it helps LeBron James offensively. LeBron is not just getting by anybody no more.
 MORE LEBRON JAMES STORIES “LeBron wants the mismatches. So now, all of a sudden, you either bring a bigger guy out on him on the perimeter, where he can get by them, or he has a smaller guy on him on the low block.
 “And you talk about a dynamic roller. LeBron James is still a hell of a screen-and-roll guy. So, if I’m Nick Nurse and I’m trying to figure out this offence, the best way to do it is go small-ball and put LeBron at the five, and then every now and then we see a sprinkle of him and Joel Embiid.”
 James has been averse to playing centre all his career, but the decision to move him there at this stage of his career isn’t very wise, despite what Perkins suggests. 
 The centres in the modern NBA are athletic as well, and the bruising in addition is something James can do without at his age. 
 If anything, a playmaking point guard role with shooters and runners around him will benefit him more. However, all these conversations based on one bad game are premature anyway.
 James doesn’t “look old” anymore. He is old, and it’s a testament to his fitness levels that he’s still contributing at such a high level. These games come with the territory at this stage of his career.
